lead.headline: BIA adds Mata Rodriguez and N-L-U- to its precedent list
lead.deck: Decisions No. 4265 (cancellation of removal for LPRs) and No. 4266 (flight risk in custody) join Volume 30.
body: The EOIR Volume 30 page, updated October 28, lists two new precedent decisions. In Matter of Mata Rodriguez, 30 I&N Dec. 191 (BIA 2026), the Board held that the Immigration Judge erred in granting discretionary cancellation of removal to a lawful permanent resident: the positive factors were outweighed by a lengthy, serious criminal history and no objective evidence of rehabilitation. In Matter of N-L-U-, 30 I&N Dec. 195 (BIA 2026), the judge erred in assessing flight risk without addressing the viability of the respondent’s marriage, the lack of a probable path to lawful status, inconsistent addresses, and the reliability of the evidence of a friend’s financial sponsorship; a pending asylum application alone does not mitigate flight risk. The page gives only the year of each decision. Read the full text before citing.

deadlines: 11/09: comments close on the OPT fee. 11/13: comments close on ending deference (I-129) and the interim refugee rule.
11/16: deadline to allege prejudice to ICE on the ratified civil penalties. 12/07: comments close on I-90 and the OPT information collection.

items.title: BIA: Matter of Mata Rodriguez, 30 I&N Dec. 191 (#4265)
items.deck: The IJ’s grant of discretionary cancellation of removal for an LPR was reversed: the equities were outweighed by a long, serious criminal record with no objective evidence of rehabilitation.
body: The IJ’s grant of discretionary cancellation of removal for an LPR was reversed: the equities were outweighed by a long, serious criminal record with no objective evidence of rehabilitation.

items.title: BIA: Matter of N-L-U-, 30 I&N Dec. 195 (#4266)
items.deck: In custody/bond review, the judge must address evidence of ties, path to status and sponsor reliability; a pending asylum application, standing alone, does not mitigate flight risk.
body: In custody/bond review, the judge must address evidence of ties, path to status and sponsor reliability; a pending asylum application, standing alone, does not mitigate flight risk.

lead.headline: BIA acrescenta Mata Rodriguez e N-L-U- à lista de precedentes
lead.deck: Decisões nº 4265 (cancelamento de remoção para LPR) e nº 4266 (risco de fuga em custódia) entram no Volume 30.
body: A página do Volume 30 do EOIR, atualizada em 28/10, lista duas decisões precedentes novas. Em Matter of Mata Rodriguez, 30 I&N Dec. 191 (BIA 2026), o Board concluiu que o juiz errou ao conceder cancelamento de remoção discricionário a residente permanente: os fatores positivos foram superados por histórico criminal longo e grave e pela ausência de prova objetiva de reabilitação. Em Matter of N-L-U-, 30 I&N Dec. 195 (BIA 2026), o juiz errou ao avaliar o risco de fuga sem tratar da viabilidade do casamento do réu, da falta de caminho provável para status legal, de endereços inconsistentes e da confiabilidade da prova de patrocínio financeiro; um pedido de asilo pendente, por si só, não reduz o risco de fuga. A página informa apenas o ano de cada decisão. Leia o texto integral antes de citar.
